headline: ‘Bottom of Your Boots’ Still Number One; Emily Ann Roberts Enters Top 5
body: [[Ella Langley]] remains atop the Hot 20 for a second week with ‘Bottom of Your Boots.’ The single is Langley’s seventh #1, and remarkably, every one of her 11 entries on the chart has reached the Top 5. Underneath Langley is [[Kenny Chesney]], who holds the #2 position for a second week with ‘Silver Sands Marina.’ It is his highest charting single since 2019’s ‘Tip of My Tongue,’ and in the coming weeks Chesney could overtake Langley for his 13th #1. The big mover this week is Kacey Musgraves’ four-week leader ‘Loneliest Girl,’ which falls 3-9. Because of this, the next six singles each climb one rung. [[Ingrid Andress]] rises 4-3 with ‘Tattoos,’ a new peak in its 15th week, while [[Kip Moore]] moves 5-4 with ‘Faith in the Wind,’ which reaches a new high in its 22nd week on the chart. New to the Top 5 is [[Emily Ann Roberts]], who rises 6-5 with ‘Laundry,’ her first career Top 5. [[Mackenzie Carpenter]] climbs 7-6 with ‘Kinda Want Your Man,’ [[The Castellows]] move 8-7 with ‘Love Is A Game’ and [[Wyatt Flores]] rises 9-8 with ‘Hate Myself,’ his first Top 10. [[Carly Pearce]] holds at #10 with ‘She Don’t.’ Just outside the Top 10, [[Riley Green]] earns the week’s Greatest Gainer trophy, jumping 14-12 with ‘Imagine That,’ while [[Kacey Musgraves]] rises 15-13 with ‘Mexico Honey,’ giving her two songs in the Top 13. There are no debuts this week, with #16 through #20 holding in place.

On the Pop 10, [[Cassandra Coleman]] holds #1 for a second week with ‘End of Your Love,’ her fifth #1 single. In fact, the entire Top 7 stays put this week, the first time that has happened in at least a year. [[Roxy Dekker]] remains at #2 with her 1-week leader ‘Ver Van M’n Bed,’ ahead of [[Karol G]]’s 1-week leader ‘Alguien Que Te Amaba’ at #3 and [[Aitana]]’s ‘6 of Febrero’ at #4, meaning three of the Top 4 are sung in a language other than English. [[Taylor Swift]] holds #5 with ‘Patient Zero.’ Interestingly, Swift has now placed eight songs on the Pop 10 but is still seeking her first #1. [[Ellie Goulding]] stays at #6 with ‘Black Prada Dress’ and [[girlsweetvoiced]] holds #7 with the three-week leader ‘Cranberry.’ Below them, [[Peach PRC]] rises 9-8 with ‘Eucalyptus’ and [[Adela]] climbs 10-9 with ‘Nicole Kidman,’ both new peaks. [[Ashe]] is the week’s only debut, entering at #10 with ‘Stop the Wedding,’ her first appearance since 2021’s #1 ‘Till Forever Falls Apart.’ Coleman’s ‘Midnight Blue’ falls off the chart from #8 to make room.
